title: Starting a tenancy in Western Australia
description: The paperwork and steps before and when a WA tenant moves in. Summarised from Consumer Protection guidance on rental agreements, condition reports and bonds.

items.title: Use the WA application to rent form if you take applications
Sign the WA residential tenancy agreement
items.detail: You can't write your own. Don't change Part B; Part C terms can't remove the tenant's rights.

items.title: Give the tenant a copy of the signed agreement within 14 days
Give the tenant the WA information for tenant sheet
Give a copy of the strata or community title by-laws
Take no more than 4 weeks' rent as bond (unless rent is over $1,200 a week), plus up to $350 pet bond if a pet is approved
Give a receipt for the bond and any rent straight away
Lodge the bond with Bonds Administration within 14 days
items.detail: Through BondsOnline, or the WA bond lodgement form if you qualify as a private landlord.

items.title: Give 2 copies of the WA property condition report within 7 days of move-in
items.detail: Take dated photos. The tenant has 7 days to return one copy.

items.title: Give a set of keys for each tenant if available
Confirm smoke alarms, RCDs and locks meet the minimum standards before move-in
